name: build-evidence-record
description: The discipline of recording claimed versus measured evidence, so a reader can tell what was observed from what was believed. Load whenever you are about to record a definition-of-done outcome or an entry in the evidence store, label a check as passing, upgrade a claim to a measurement, cite evidence inside a skill, or reconcile a measurement that contradicts what the design says: it fixes what an evidence record contains (what was run, the code version and tree hash under test, whether the tree was dirty, the output, the status label), how records are appended and chained so an edit is detectable, and what a contradicting measurement obliges you to do.

purpose.text: Record what was actually run, against which code version, and what came back, so a claim is never laundered into a measurement by rewording.

shapes.name: evidence-record (proposed shape; summary - the full schema with per-field constraints and the dirty-tree rule is in references/evidence-record-shape.md)
shapes.quote: Each record names the script SHA-256, git commit, tree hash under test, and whether the tree was dirty

invariants.text: Every record names what was run and the code version it ran against: the hash of the script and the commit.
invariants.quote: Each record names the script SHA-256, git commit

invariants.text: Every record names the tree that was actually under test and whether that tree was dirty, because a dirty tree is not the commit.
invariants.quote: tree hash under test, and whether the tree was dirty

invariants.text: Every record carries exactly one status label, claimed or measured. An absent label is a defect, not a default.

Proposed: a result produced from a dirty tree may never carry the label measured, because nobody else can reproduce the tree it ran against. Research query: unresearched beyond the dirty flag the evidence store already records (F-a5-04); no prior-art search has been run for the reproducibility rationale specifically.
The store is append-only. A record is never edited or deleted; a correction is a new record naming the id of the one it supersedes.
records are chained the way the hash-chained task store is, so that each run's closing digest is the next run's opening digest, so a manual edit between runs is detectable.
invariants.quote: each run's closing digest is the next run's opening digest, so a manual edit between runs is detectable

invariants.text: Proposed: the record holds the output as observed, with its exit status, not a summary of it. A summary cannot be re-read against a later run. Research query: unresearched; our own convention, no prior-art search has been run for a raw-output-over-summary requirement in evidence record keeping.

Proposed: measured is a property of an attached run, not of confidence. A record with no run attached is claimed by construction, however certain its author is. Research query: unresearched; our own convention, no prior-art search has been run for a run-attachment (versus author confidence) definition of a measured label.

not_exposed.text: This discipline does not produce a signed attestation for a third party. It records what happened for a reader of this repo; attributing an artifact to the code, inputs and actor that produced it, verifiable with a tool we did not write, is the provenance concern's job and is deliberately kept separate.
not_exposed.quote: verifiable with a tool we did not write

instructions.action: Write the claim down before you run anything, in the words you intend to publish, and give it a record id. Research query: unresearched; our own convention, no prior-art search has been run for a write-the-claim-before-the-run requirement in evidence or audit-trail record keeping.
instructions.why: Proposed: our convention. A claim written after the output is read is shaped by the output, and the record can no longer show what was believed beforehand.

instructions.action: Capture run identity before the run and record it as data, not as a description: the exact command, the SHA-256 of the script it invoked, the commit, the hash of the tree actually under test, and whether that tree was dirty.
instructions.why: These are the fields the evidence store already records. A description cannot be re-run, the script hash pins the thing that produced the output after the script changes, and the dirty flag separates a reproducible result from an unreproducible one.
instructions.quote: Each record names the script SHA-256, git commit, tree hash under test, and whether the tree was dirty

instructions.action: Capture the output as observed, with its exit status, into the record. Truncate at the end if you must; do not paraphrase, reorder, or clean it up. Research query: unresearched; our own convention, no prior-art search has been run for a no-paraphrase raw-output-capture rule in evidence record keeping.
instructions.why: Proposed: our convention. The record's only job is to let a later reader see what you saw, including the parts that did not fit the claim.

instructions.action: Label the record claimed or measured. Use measured only when this record carries a run: a command, a code version, a clean tree, an exit status and the output. Everything else, including a confident inference, is claimed.
instructions.why: The whole point of the two labels is that a reader can separate what was observed from what was believed.

instructions.action: Refuse the label measured when the tree was dirty. Append the record as claimed and say in the claim text that the tree was dirty; re-run on a clean tree if the measurement matters. Research query: unresearched beyond the dirty flag the evidence store already records (F-a5-04); no prior-art search has been run for a reproducibility-gated label specifically.
instructions.why: Proposed: our convention, following the dirty flag the evidence store records. A result nobody can reproduce is a report of an event, not a measurement of the code.

instructions.action: Correct a record only by appending another, since the evidence store is append-only JSONL: to upgrade a claim to measured, append a record that attaches a run; when a measurement contradicts a claim, append the measurement. Either way name the old record's id in supersedes, and never rewrite, reword or delete the record being corrected.
instructions.why: Proposed: our convention on an append-only store. An in-place relabel leaves no trace of when a belief became an observation, and each recorded finding invalidates a design that looks correct on paper, so the superseded claim is what shows the next reader which paper-correct designs have already failed.

instructions.action: Append every record, chain it to its predecessor, and carry the closing digest of a run into the opening digest of the next.
instructions.why: A chain makes a manual edit between runs detectable, which is what stops a record being quietly improved after the fact.
instructions.quote: each run's closing digest is the next run's opening digest, so a manual edit between runs is detectable

instructions.action: Verify the chain and the source hash with `python3 tools/kb.py verify` before citing any record, stop if it fails, and cite as one or more kb ids plus a quote copied character for character out of one cited record via `python3 tools/kb.py show <id>`. Research query: unresearched beyond the task store's own chain-verification property (F-a5-03); no prior-art search has been run for cite-then-verify as a citation discipline specifically.
instructions.why: Proposed: our convention. An unverified record is a claim about a record, and a restatement from memory is how a claim acquires the authority of a measurement it never had.
instructions.quote: a manual edit between runs is detectable

instructions.action: Scope the measured label to what the run observed, and no wider: name the property that was checked, not the property you hope it stands for.
instructions.why: A pipeline can run green with every behavioural stage skipped; those establish well-formedness, not correctness.

instructions.action: Proposed: read references/evidence-record-shape.md before implementing or checking the record store itself - writing the writer, writing the validator, or reviewing a record whose fields are present but whose values look wrong. The skill body is enough to write a record by hand.
instructions.why: Proposed reference material. It holds the full field-level schema and the dirty-tree rule, which is too long to sit in this table and is needed only when the store is being built rather than used.

best_practices.text: Record what the receiving side reported, not what was sent: injected context was ignored downstream and a depth-3 task tree produced three unrelated root traces, so a record of the injection would have been evidence of nothing.
best_practices.quote: A depth-3 task tree produces three unrelated root traces.

best_practices.text: Measure the runtime effect, not the file you wrote: configuration written in the documented place validated, reviewed correctly, and had no runtime effect at all.
best_practices.quote: Values written to YAML validated, reviewed correctly, and had no runtime effect

best_practices.text: Treat an automated verification that reports all currently green as a claim about the check until a record attaches the run that produced it.
best_practices.quote: each with automated verification, all currently green

best_practices.text: Say where and when a measurement was taken, the way the inventory does when it says it was verified against the running host on 2026-09-03; a measurement with no place and no date cannot be re-taken.
best_practices.quote: verified against the running host on 2026-09-03

best_practices.text: prefer few records that each name their code version to many that do not. A store of ~2,445 records across 308 runs is worth only the fraction of records whose run identity is complete.

definition_of_done.criterion: python3 tools/kb.py verify && python3 -c "import json;rs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('kb/facts.jsonl')];assert rs and all(r.get('status') for r in rs);print('labels ok',len(rs))"
definition_of_done.expected: Two checks over the record store: (1) integrity via tools/kb.py verify; (2) labelling, which asserts records_checked > 0 and unlabelled == 0. Check 1 prints 'kb verified: chains intact, source hash matches, every fact matches its lines, rebuild is identical' and exits 0. Check 2 prints 'labels ok 109' and exits 0.
definition_of_done.breakage: Two, applied one at a time to kb/facts.jsonl and then restored: (a) mismatched hash — change one character of record F-a5-04's text ('Append-only' to 'Append-Only') so the record no longer hashes to its stored digest; (b) missing status — delete the status field from record F-a5-04.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: Measured in this session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01XDYnrM4HZbMdASzsqN4j96) on 2026-09-03 in /home/user/AGENT. Breakage (a): check 1 printed 'FAIL: chain broken at facts F-a5-04', 'FAIL: F-a5-04 text does not match PASS.md lines 77-77', 'kb verification FAILED' and exited 1. Breakage (b): check 2 printed 'records 109 unlabelled 1 [F-a5-04]', raised AssertionError and exited 1, and check 1 printed 'FAIL: chain broken at facts F-a5-04' and exited 1, because the label is inside the hashed record. After restoring kb/facts.jsonl (sha256 a95803f63e274d768144ef05825a27c0646b0fe3ffbe7b49c28fcac52fc27950, git tree clean) both checks exited 0.
definition_of_done.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

measured_run.clean_output:
kb verified: chains intact, source hash matches, every fact matches its lines, rebuild is identical
labels ok 109
measured_run.breakage_output:
FAIL: chain broken at facts F-a5-04
kb verification FAILED

open_questions.question: Are the records in the evidence store chained, or only appended? The source states append-only for the evidence store and hash-chaining only for the task store, so the chain invariant here is ours rather than a description of what runs.
open_questions.evidence: Reading the evidence store on the running host and checking whether each record carries a predecessor digest; this agent has no access to that host, so nothing here can be measured.
open_questions.default: The chain requirement is recorded as proposed, and an evidence record is treated as unverified until a chain verification passes.

open_questions.question: What counts as the tree hash when the run touches files outside the repository, for example a configuration read from the host?
open_questions.evidence: A run recorded twice with the same commit and tree hash but different host state, showing whether the outputs diverge; the divergence would decide whether host state must be a required field.
open_questions.default: Proposed: such a run is labelled claimed, and the record names the outside input it depended on.
